name: PLOT_Ceres_Ask_Prove_BCER
title: Ask How You Prove Yourself
desc:
You approach Pan Tao at his usual smoking spot and ask him how someone like you can prove your loyalty to the Titan cause.  

"Few options," Tao says. "First is territory. The whole belt is in a kind of King of the Hill situation. If you trade for a Titan beacon, you can take it out to unclaimed space near some profitable asteroids. Deploy it and we have eyes on those rocks. Keeps our supply lines open."

"Xinhua likes to throw out their own beacons, so you could always blow those up. That's kinda fun, and the brass gets a big kick out of it."

"If you're feeling froggy, you could always jump. By that I mean: sieze or destroy a Xinhua allied vessel. Demand their surrender or, ya know. Boom."

"Lastly, you can hit the mines. Plenty of good rocks left. Get some ore and sell it to one of our faction kiosks here. That gets you good scrip, plus attaboys from the right folks. 

"Besides that, you could try and run special missions for Mr. Wayne. He doesn't give them to everybody, so if he trusts you to handle it, it's probably a good bet. Check the planter up near 'The Mouth' for messages."

name: PLOT_Ceres_Ask_Prove_BCRS
title: Ask How You Prove Yourself
desc:
You approach Francisco Ortega. He's looking jumpy as usual. Careful as you can, you ask how someone like you can prove your loyalty to the Xinhua cause.  

"You have a few options,"  Ortega starts.

"First is territory. The whole belt is in open conflict. Might makes right. If you trade for a Xinhua beacon, you can take it out to unclaimed space near some profitable asteroids. Deploy it and we have eyes on those rocks. Keeps our supply lines open."

"Titan's deploying their own beacons, you could neutralize them - so long as you feel safe in enemy territory."

"The cause can always use able pilots. If you're feeling brave, you can sieze or destroy a Titan allied vessel. Demand their surrender, or take them out by force."

"Lastly, mining. The belt is rich. If you find some ore, you can sell it to one of our faction kiosks here. That gets you scrip for more weapons and beacons, and it helps fill our coffers."

"Besides that, you could try and run special ... errands for our mutual friend. Check the coffee machine. It's a dead drop, so we don't have to keep meeting like this."

name: ENCFirstDockBCRSInfo
title: Get Your Bearings
desc: As you try to work out where you've been deposited, you hear a raspy voice at your shoulder: "Got a light?" A funny little woman waves an unlit Viceroy at you. She has thick white eyebrows, thick black framed glasses, and an accent you cannot place. She doesn't look like the hawkers you narrowly escaped. "Are you going to try to sell me something?" you ask. She gestures with the cigarette. "Probably not." Once the cigarette is lit, she takes a satisfied drag, exhaling a long stream through her nostrils. "You're just off the [us-shipname], correct?" "How did you know that?" "Relax," she says airily. "It's all anyone talks about on the Ring. Every miner here is a fat walking bag of money, and everyone else wants some. Retail surveillance is building your personality profile as we speak. Face, name, how long you'd glance at her tits," she indicates an erotic advertisement you've not yet seen, "how many steps you've taken, where you stopped, where you've come from, where you're going." She gives you a pause to chew on that, then indicates herself. "Eleni Konstantinidis. I'm a trader, like you, of a sort. Us ship captains look out for one another. Let me buy you a coffee."

name: ENCFirstDockBCRSInfoAccept
title: Accept
desc:
Despite her stated lack of interest in selling you anything, or perhaps because of it, you're wary. You follow her unerring footsteps just off the concourse to an equally crowded but less rancidly desperate intersection, and into a dimly lit coffee house there.

Low lighting, better acoustics, and the return of your personal space are all immediate and ongoing reliefs. The clientele resemble Eleni in demeanour if not in look: serious men and women sit one-on-one in private booths, engaged in fierce but inaudible debate. The real deals are made here.

Eleni banters briefly in Greek with the host, who seats you at her favourite booth.

"Let's start with the basics of life in Ceres space," she says, "and this will go much quicker if you ask me about what you don't know than I try to guess. Like the war. You know about the war?"

"I don't know," you say. "Do I?"

"Exactly," says Eleni. "So ask me about the war. Thank you, Niko." The host puts a fresh pot and two china cups between you. You take a sip, and have to stop yourself from spilling in surprise, without contest, the best coffee you've ever tasted.

name: ENCFirstDockBCRSInfoAskWar
title: Ask her about the war
desc: Eleni fiddles with her necklace, shifting the pearls along the string with one hand. It's a chintzy fake, in your estimation. Perhaps it has sentimental value. "It's like this. Mars and Titan - Xinhua and the United States. They got all the money. They want, they need, metal. There's metal out there, all over, oodles of it, sitting in the asteroids. In the Belt, Jupiter, doesn't matter. But they got problems. It's an ocean of soup, and they've both got tiny little plastic spoons." She holds up a complimentary tiny plastic spoon wrapped in utensil package, and tosses it aside. "Ever tried cracking an asteroid, gathering up all the dust and rock, sifting through it all for the shit that isn't worthless? And then, you've got a fuckload of kamacite and your dick in your hands, but you want a steel coil you can sell. Have you got a blast furnace and water enough to swim in?" She doesn't wait for you to answer. "Fuck that noise. It's expensive, time-consuming, and dangerous. They'd much rather us do it for them." "I'm familiar with mining," you say. "Then you'll be familiar with how mining ships go missing around here," she says flatly, "and by 'go missing', I mean they were last seen entering the torpedo envelope of an unaligned ship before suffering complete existence failure. They're not fucking around, my young friend. There's a killing to be made here." She leans forward, peering over her glasses as they ever so slightly slip down her nose. "Be sure the killing's not made of you." "Nice." "Thank you." She sips her coffee.

name: ENCFirstDockBCRSInfoAskWar2
title: Ask her who's doing the killing
desc:
Eleni dips her finger in the saucer. She draws on the placemat: Ring station, and its parent body Ceres, which both look unhelpfully like messy brown coffee circles. She draws another one, big, with a bunch of dots. 

"That's us, Ring Station and Ceres, and that's them, King Jupiter and his moons. As sure as they're here in secret, blasting us to pieces whenever we're nodding off behind the wheel, our brave boys and girls are over there doing the same to the Galileans."

"The station can't stop the Galileans operating here?"

"The station is trying," she says. "Everyone living in Calico City is sick of the corporate yoke, and they're the Coalition's main source of miners. There's a sliver of overlap in the Venn diagram between those pissed off folks and all the happy-go-lucky sods on the concourse outside, in that Bosch painting," she says. You nod like you've seen the painting before, or for that matter, any painting before. Aren't paintings supposed to be beautiful?

"If they push too hard, the people will push back. And the Coalition will find themselves with another revolution, right here on their front doorstep."

name: ENCFirstDockBCRSInfoAskWar3
title: Ask why the Galileans care so much
desc:
"Bigger picture," you ask, "why's the competition so fierce? Why blow up each other's ships?"

"It's the economy, stupid." You frown. She smiles indulgently, as if to a favoured child. "Look it up sometime, I'm not calling you stupid. All wars are fought for money, or things that turn into money, like power or control or slaves. Ceres and Jupiter are selling all this stuff to Mars and Titan, and whoever secures the Belt can starve their opponent."

"Xinhua controls the Coalition, by complicated financial wizardry. Every corp with a stake, if you dig enough, is partly or wholly owned by someone else and someone else, et cetera, far back until you get to Xinhua."

"And Titan?"

"Jupiter," she says, "or, the Galilean Confederacy, they're calling it these days. They've got more moons than brain cells. Overthrew the Troy-Jupiter Group, declared for themselves, and now Titan's the only thing propping them up. Your guess is as good as mine whether they make it five years, or five more weeks."

"So I've got it clear," you say slowly, "you're saying that Xinhua and the US are in a cold war to control the Belt, but the prize in controlling the Belt, is that it would help win a war over the Belt?"

She mulls over the sentence, then raises her hand to the host for a refill. "That's pretty much it," she says.

name: ENCFirstDockBCRSInfoRefuse
title: Refuse
desc:
"Suit yourself," she says. Without missing a beat she veers into the nearest brothel.

Time-to-shop, indeed.

name: CruzCall
title: A Message Squared
desc:
In your inbox, you find a message for a message: ZaraFone, an odd little outfit which provides a professional, comfortable setting for interplanetary communication, has a video waiting for you, sender withheld. And of course you may not watch it on your device, no; you must go there physically and sit in a booth and commune. How else can they profit?

When you get a few minutes to yourself, you pass by ZaraPhone. A clerk shows you to your booth, activates an incense vaporiser, and leaves a hot pouch of green tea slowly spinning in the air by your shoulder. They close the door behind them.

The lights dim. Your pleather chair has a chunky keyboard in one arm, with which you instruct the room to play the message.

name: CruzCall2
title: Isambard Returns
desc: Isamard snaps into existence on the screen. She's in a recording booth of her own, but whether that's next door or another planet is impossible to know. "Hello, young [us-custom-characterGenderCond|man|lady|... person]. It is me: Isambard Cruz! We met not long ago. Did not talk much, but sometimes, is how strong bonds are forged." She has storage bricks piled nearby, all set to travel mode. Her cat is in a pet carrier atop the pile. "And you showed polite interest in Jomari. That counts a lot." She sniffs. "I watched the tape you found. Perhaps I am a hypocrite. Don't care. Not important. The tape, it worries me. Abacho and friends are in danger. With the law and ... with others. Avoid them. Or," she shrugs with a quirk of her mouth, "go see them. Is your funeral." Not the best timing. Would it have killed her to call when you were both on station? ... Did she think it would?

name: CruzCall3
title: Cruz' Cruise
desc:
Isambard continues after a moment, developing a cryptic little grin. "I have a clue for you, if you avoid funeral. I recognise a man in the video. The student in the classroom, put camera up his nose. He work for me many years ago. He was older - he is older now too - but is him, I am certain. Benjamin Choong," she says, enunciating clearly, and repeats it for emphasis. "With two o's."

"He lives on Ring Station at Ceres, in the old hub. He won't return my message ... I have address. Take your ship, fly to Ceres, go to his apartment. Maybe he tell you why his private video was on mysterious VHS. And you do wellness check. Leave reply for me with ZaraFone, please."

She reaches without looking and rubs her cat - Jomari? - Jomari's head through the carrier bars. "I would go, but I fear the danger will come for me too. Instead I go where no one will look. Therefore I need itinerant ship detective - and here you are! Too perfect arrangement not to ask."

She smiles ruefully. "Having watched this message, you are plus two hundred thousand US dollars. Use it to get to Ceres - any remainder, you keep. If you take the money but don't go, you are bad person, and will meet a sticky end. All right. Good luck. Good bye now." She hits a button, and the video ends. Not one for ceremony.

name: CruzCall4
title: A New Ceres
desc:
You check your account. As promised it's healthier by two hundred grand. And all it cost was the threat of a curse from an old Filipina.

As leads go, it's slim. As incentives go, it's weak. But it's all you've got. If you want to find out who made that tape, it looks like you've got to get your ass to Ceres.

name: Plot_Scholar_Flat_ContinueLooking
title: Continue Looking
desc: You return to a central location in the apartment and look around, deciding where to search next.

name: Plot_Scholar_Flat_Enter1
title: Have another look
desc: You return to Choong's apartment, wondering if there's something you might have missed. You look around, wondering where to check first.

name: ENCFirstDockBCERCalico
title: Enter Calico
desc:
You spend some time watching the city at work, gripping a safety railing by the terminal overlook. It's the only such safety device you can see. The Ceresians seem very comfortable floating themselves from building to building, sailing through unmarked volumes that they somehow know are for public transit, without ever once colliding. A helpful plaque advises that visitors and non-residents use software assistance to travel these arteries.

Before too long, as you follow the luminous floating arrows overlaid in your PDA's viewfinder, you have your first collision. There are two types of traveling Ceresians: single, harried looking salarymen, and gaggles of youths bantering in American drawls. It's the latter that you hit, though you could've sworn you were following your arrow correctly. Somehow a limb gets hooked and then you smack through the middle of them like a bowling ball.

Their voices turn from loud and happy to shrill and angry. A tall boy in a polo shirt emblazoned with a scowling Vegeta disentangles himself from his friends. He floats toward you, stopping gracefully with a blast from his wrist jets. "Hey, Offworld," he says, and it's clearly meant as a disparaging form of address. "You made a mistake just now. You mind apologising to my friends, here?"

His right hand crosses to his left hip. A twitch of his fingers pulls his shirt back just enough to reveal the distinctive wooden grip of a Colt 1911 poking out the waistband of his jeans.

name: ENCFirstDockBCERCalicoApologise
title: Apologise
desc:
"It was totally my fault," you say. "I don't know how to get around yet. I hope nobody was hurt."

"Mm," he says, considering. "That dog ain't gonna hunt." His friends, now reformed as a group of eager spectators, giggle and snicker.

"Someone oughta teach you how to apologise properly, Offworld," he says, gripping the pistol butt in hand. "Someone like me."

"Sure, if you're good at apologising, you can give me some pointers," you say. The laughter from his friends stops. Uh-oh. It turns out their brains are developed enough to detect irony.

He draws the gun. His followers sigh happily. His hand is down for now, but his eyes - his eyes are pinpricks of rage. What the hell is this kid's problem?

"Beg, Offworld," he says. "Beg for your life."

name: ENCFirstDockBCERCalicoBeg
title: Beg
desc: "Please don't kill me," you say fervently. "I really, really, really don't want to die, and not like this, not over some accident." "Not like this?" he repeats, incensed. "It would be an honour to die by my hand. I've sent four souls to Hell. Wish you to join them?" Christ, now he's talking like a Shakespeare villain. "No, no sir," you say smartly. Beyond your tunnel vision on this psychopathic teen brandishing a museum piece, you can sense the flow of street traffic ignoring the street drama with uncanny propriety. "I wish not to dishonour you by wasting your bullet on worthless offworld trash like myself." He cocks his head. "That wasn't half bad, in truth." One of his lackeys nods sincerely. "Okay. I'll spare your miserable life. But maybe I'll put one arm out of commission, so you don't forget." He takes aim, his gun hand drifting lazily down to target your shoulder.

name: ENCFirstDockBCERCalicoAuntLiz
title: Continue
desc:
"CHADWICK O'NEILL," bellows a woman's voice from above. The tall youth - Chadwick - cringes at once, and the gun is no longer pointed at you. You release a breath you didn't know you'd held.

A short older woman - though she couldn't be much past forty - swoops down like an angel. She plants herself in front of Chadwick, who can't meet her look. His friends begin drifting away in ones and twos. "What would your mother say if she saw you mistreating this clumsy foreigner? What about your father, Heaven rest his soul?"

"It wasn't like that, Aunt Liz," Chadwick says to the ground. "I was only -"

Aunt Liz smacks him backhand across the face. It's not for show. She's wearing rings. Blood spirals away toward the city lights. She hits him again exactly as hard. When he raises his head, he already has a bruise. His murderous exterior is shattered, and a frightened child peers through it.

"Go to your room," she says. Quietly said, but somehow the entire street will have heard it. Chadwick backs up as fast as he can, flipping and shooting off on his gas jets without any of his former grace.

Aunt Liz - presumably Liz, to you - drifts over to her second priority. "Thank you," you say. "I don't know what I did, but -"

"Silence, Offworld," she says. There's no venom to it, but it's much more cutting than when her nephew said it. "I am speaking. If you do not have one, buy a gun and carry it openly. Without it you will invite duels, or unwanted sexual attention."

"Are you serious?" you say.

"Yes," she says. "It would be best for you to handle your business here, and depart from Calico as soon as you are able."

She turns on one heel jet and leaves.

name: ENCFirstDockBCRSInfoAskCalico
title: Ask about Ceres and Calico City
desc:
"Calico City is kind of a crazy place, right?" you say.

"What do you expect? An American colony abandoned by its creditors long ago; then along comes Xinhua." She shrugs. "Isolated, xenophobic, kept in arrested development by a foreign superpower, desperately clutching to their myths of a glorious past - all things considered, and taking the long view, they're quite a normal people. They've been taught to worship a way of life that never was ..." 

She lingers on the thought, then plows on a little more brusquely. "Fucked up is normal, on this world stage of ours." She leans forward and whispers a secret to you. "The hot springs are divine. Cryovolcanic mineral water is very good for the skin."

"I'll have to check those out," you say.

"Mm, well, make sure you're armed at all times. They like their cowboy movies. If you offend someone -" she cocks a finger-pistol at you. "Pew! Pew, pew!" 

Perhaps some people never get the hang of onomatopoeia.

name: ENCFirstDockBCRSInfoAskGalCon
title: Ask about the Galilean Confederacy
desc:
"What's the story with the Galilean Confederacy?"

"Oof, where to begin," she says. "You know about Troy-Jupiter, all that?"

"Kind of," you say.

"You might've seen them in the headlines a few years back. The Troy-Jupiter Group. Local oligarchs of Jupiter; most of it, anyway, twenty moons' worth. A cautionary tale," she wags a finger, "on how much one may starve the serfdom before they do something about it."

"Food was that scarce?" you say doubtfully.

"Of course it wasn't," she says. She smiles. "Well, not that scarce. A few shipments went missing that really ought to have made it there. Regardless, who do you think was first on half rations?"

"The executives and their families, as a way of gracefully admitting fault," you say. Eleni snorts. "Probably law enforcement too, to show solidarity."

"The latter actually happened," she says, "and that's how we got the Galilean Confederacy, and why Troy-Jupiter is no more."

name: ENCFirstDockBCERCalicoHoldYourGround
title: Hold your ground
desc:
"I'm not apologising for anything," you say. "You ran into me. I saw the whole thing - I was there."

He draws the piece. "I have to burn this shirt," he says thoughtfully. "Because it got Offworld sweat on it, or it got Offworld blood on it." He levels it at you. "The choice is yours. Beg, Offworld."

name: ENCFirstDockBCERCalicoCarrying
title: Show you're carrying, too
desc:
You let your hand drift to your armament, too.

"If I made a mistake, it won't be me who pays for it," you say evenly. "Your friends look like adults." A harmless untruth. "If they're injured, they can speak for themselves."

You lock eyes. It's not hard to get the measure of him. He needs to save face, and if you back down, he can't. He breaks his gaze first. He grins boyishly at his crew, who look none the worse for wear.

"I think we're good here," he says. Suddenly he's friendly, even charming. "Welcome to Calico, friend. We hope you enjoy your visit."

They retreat in good order. Nobody on the street has batted an eyelid.

What the hell is wrong with this place?

name: ENCFirstDockBCERCalicoBegIronically
title: Beg more ironically still
desc: "Sure, I can do this," you say. "Do you guys lick boots here? Where do you stand on boots?" A vein pulses in his forehead. "Okay, not that. How about this: I'll make it up to you. Call your mother. I'll take her out to dinner. Treat her right, pay for everything, eat her box, call her in the morning." Damn, whispers one of the posse, in reverence or disgust. You spread your hands. "Well? Where's my bullet, guy? I've got somewhere to be." Tears forming at the corner of his eyes, he lowers the gun. He drifts away, shoulders hunched. One of the girls swoops after him, concerned. Dollars to donuts, that thing was a replica. Or unloaded. You look at his retreating back, annoyed as you are mystified. One of his friends passes you, reproachful look on his face. "Not cool," he says. "Chad's going through a tough time right now." You nod, nonplussed. To reply would be a waste of effort.

name: PLOT_Ceres_The_Scholar_Establish_Contact_CCRE_Reply_Encounter_GalGon_Loyalty_More
title: Ask What In God's Name He Is Talking About
desc:
"Moles, fucknuts! Xinhua rats. Place is lousy with 'em. Sometimes we scare 'em up hackin and other times, well. Measures more drastic, if you get my meaning."

"Now here's how you suss 'em out," Wayne leans in so close you can smell the Bismertnaya on his breath. "They train em up good back on Mars. Computer shit, like I said, but fightin' too. Hand to hand, real close quarters. They like to get in and out unseen, so keep an eye out for the sneaky ones. They're cruel little bastards, but they aren't dumb. Most of em are a hell of a lot smarter than me, and that's sayin' something."

"Anyway," he says. "You meet someone like that, more than likely that's our mole. Drop your half of the Xinhua code phrase and if they know the rest, well? That would mean somethin', wouldn't it?"

name: PLOT_Ceres_The_Scholar_Establish_Contact_CCRE_Reply_Encounter_GalGon_Loyalty_Codes
title: Ask About Code Phrase
desc:
"Lemme ask you: Where is true west?"

"Depends where you're standing," you respond.

"Nope. Where is true west?" he asks again.

You hesitate to answer.

"Personally, I'd say to follow the evening redness. But that's just me," Wayne says, and gives you a wink.

"So, the dead drop," Wayne continues. "You know the embassy on this station? There's a ship and home kiosks next door with a planter in the corner. Ficus or some shit. If you really want to show loyalty to God's Great GalCon, rummage around in there, sneaky beaky like. Had to move that thing like ten times last month and honestly I'm gettin' a little tired of it."

Wayne leans back, tips his cap and holds up two more fingers. "Shot for the road?"

He drains the little cup like he's done it a million times before. You eye your own drink with obvious suspicion, given the circumstances. 

"More for me then, I guess," he says, and drinks your glass down before sauntering out of the bar without paying.

name: PLOT_Ceres_The_Scholar_Discuss_Tradecraft
title: Discuss Tradecraft
desc:
Pan Tao rolls his eyes at your approach, then lights a new cigarette using his first. "How'd that go?" he asks without looking at you.

"About as well as you'd expect," you reply.

Pan Tao frowns and nods. "Yeah," he says. "Wayne loves his little 'aw-shucks' hayseed act. Don't let it fool you. Guy probably has eyes on us right now."  

Less attitude than before, at least. Helpful, even.

name: PLOT_Ceres_The_Scholar_Discuss_Tradecraft_Mole
title: Ask About The Mole
desc:
"If there even is one," Pan says. "Rumors, hearsay. Every drunk on this rock has a story. I've damn near lost track."

"Tell me one," you say.

"Well. Couple days ago an atmo system near residential hit the fritz, right? Not so abnormal at first. The station is a shithole. But then, all the way across the rock, another one went down. Then another. You see where this is going."

"Not a coincidence," you reply.

"Could be! That's the rub. Look, if there's really a Xinhua rat this deep in our network, they'd be smart. Very smart. A skilled enough hacker to do that and more. They'd know how to talk, too. Good with oligarchs, good with the military brass. A real 'friend to all' type. Otherwise, how would they get access to intel?"

Useful. "Any other advice?" you ask.

"Shit," he says. "We didn't even have this conversation."

name: PLOT_Ceres_The_Scholar_Discuss_Tradecraft_Wetwork
title: Get Wetwork Advice
desc: "A fellow painter I see," Pan says. "I'll tell you what I tell everyone: start with the exit plan. Things always go down faster than you think. Once the deed is done, I mean."

name: PLOT_Ceres_The_Scholar_Discuss_Tradecraft_Blackhat
title: Get Blackhat Advice
desc: "Not my area," Pan says. "I'm more of a hands-on kinda guy."

name: ENCFirstDockBCRSHmm
title: Something is bothering you
desc:
"Sorry, can we run this back?" you say. Something is bothering you. Something niggling at the edge of memory and time.

"Mm? To what, or where, my friend?" She smiles.

"It was something you said before," you say. She's playing with her necklace again. The glassy pearls sliding along the string, clinking softly as they rub against their mates.

What was it she said? Something about Calico City. "I'm sorry," you say, blinking. "It's not coming to me, whatever it is."

"That's perfectly alright."

name: ENCFirstDockBCRSHmm1
title: Have we met before?
desc:
"Have we met before?" you ask her suddenly. You don't think you have - it's a sensation, an impression, rather than a recollection. Perhaps you've met her sister. "Have you ever been to K-Leg?"

"Oh, certainly not," she says. "I've been there once or twice, but I would remember if we had crossed paths."

"That makes sense," you say. "Yeah. Forget I asked."

name: ENCFirstDockBCRSLeave
title: Go your separate ways
desc:
Your encounter with Eleni ends there, on that note, with only the customary sorting of payment and debt to plow through - a neutral and empty space, in contrast to the strangeness of the whole sit-down. She insists on paying. You let her, and promise to get the next one, which is never going to happen.

You amble back to the concourse to bid your final goodbyes. The desperation of the shoppers and the sellers seems muted now, and no more greeters try to inveigle you into their stores, such is the change in your aura.

"Be seeing you," Eleni says. She makes a curious circle gesture with one hand - a goodbye? - and is gone.

What an odd duck.

name: ENCFirstDockBCRSHmm3
title: Really try to remember
desc:
"Scratch that," you say, "don't forget I asked. I want to nail this down, whatever it is."

"Mm?" she says, smiling politely, meaninglessly.

That's it. That's what it is.

"You said," you say slowly. It's as if you're on the cusp of waking. The words are there, but struggling to be said. "You said the Calicoans ..."

"Yes," she says unhappily.

"You said they were taught to worship a way of life that never was ..."

"I did," she says. "I did say that." She scowls. But it's just an expression. There's no feeling behind it.

"A man on K-Leg said something very similar to me before I left," you say.

She waves a hand questioningly.

name: ENCFirstDockBCRSHmm4
title: Make an outrageous accusation
desc:
"I'm going to ask again," you say. "Tell me the truth. Do I know you?"

Eleni stops fidgeting with her necklace, and places her hands in her lap. "Well, now. That's one question I can't help you with."

Her eyes, behind her thick glasses, are magnified like a bug's. The overblown pupils reach the hard edges of the frame as they dart around, scanning the room. They recentre, and she fixes you with a strangely steely gaze.

Inside that steel, a trace of gold.

The word comes unbidden to your lips, and once arrived, refuses to leave. It doesn't make sense, and yet out it comes. "... Smiley?"

The question hangs between you like a smart munition searching for a target.

She smiles at you. No more maternal beneficence. It recalls Smiley's fixed, dopey trademark - but with a new element, a wildcard that turns the wide silly expression predatory.

"It's me. In the flesh," she - he? They? - says, and sighs. "The flesh and like 3 kilos of silicone prosthetics, anyway. Shit. [us-firstname], how've you been?"

"How have I been?" you say hollowly. "Fuck you. Whoever you are, go fuck yourself. What is going on?"

"I'm trying to help you," she says - you settle on she for now, with nothing else to go on. "You wandered away from K-LEG and wound up at Ceres, from the frying pan into the fire, truly. And I suppose I have a soft spot for a fellow AV Clubber."

"I want nothing more to do with you." You stand up. Heads turn your way. You're not bothering to lower your voice.

"Sit down," she says levelly. One of her hands, under the table, tracks your every movement. 

You ease back into your chair. You've seen people in similar situations, in crowded rooms on K-LEG. You try desperately to remember how they ended.

"Thank you," she says conversationally, as if you had passed her a sauce packet. She runs a tongue along her teeth, then reaches into her mouth. She spits into her hand, and tosses a large set of dentures onto the table. The long white teeth drip, saliva strung between the points.

"That," she says, again running a tongue around her mouth, "was driving me crazy."

title: Continue
desc: "What happens now?" you ask. "We're just talking," she says. It's surreal: the silver haired woman is perfectly convincing, even now you know - well, what do you know? "Talking normally, calmly. Let's not put Niko out. I had to learn Greek for this bit, I don't want to burn it." "So you're not Greek." "I am not." "Then what?" "An Episcopalian." She shrugs. "What's it to you?" "You got all your 'friends' on K-Leg killed, or shipped off to Prokofiev," you hiss. "Nearly me, too. That's what it is to me." "That," she says, appearing a little hurt, "was not my fault. That was quite a setback for me, actually. I'm picking up the pieces." "You think you're a victim in all this?" "I didn't say that," she says, smiling hungrily. "It's that old adage - you know, 'nobody thinks of themselves as a villain'. Right? When an adult says it to a child, they're implying: 'therefore, because it's relative, there's no such thing as a villain!' An early pitfall in your conception of other people, and people shoot right on into adulthood without revisiting it." You stare across at the table. "What the fuck are you talking about?" "I'm trying to say, a single counterexample torpedoes the whole thing." She points to herself. "And that's me. I'm the counterexample." You don't want to repeat yourself, so you think of the next most pertinent question. "Can I go now?" Smiley, Eleni, whoever she is, edges out of the booth first. "Way ahead of you. It's on my tab." You can see the pistol now. At least you weren't falling for a bluff - that's nice to know. She stows it under her coat. "I really was trying to help," she says. "Be seeing you." She slips out of the cafe. The host looks up at her departure, frowning. You finish your coffee, trying to shake a sudden attack of depersonalisation. The videotape ... not for the first time since K-Leg, you wish you'd never found it.
